elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 4.1 retains "This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" with no mutual-written-agreement requirement, and the conditional preferred elements (30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder) are not all satisfied.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — one-year renewal term, unchanged by the edit.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered text sets the Company's window at "sixty (60) ... days written notice", which exceeds the preferred 30-day opt-out.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in rendered Section 4.1; the drafter expressly declined to press it in the comment.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Conditional trigger does not apply: consideration is a fixed 30% revenue share (Section 3.1) and Section 4.1 contains no renewal price-uplift mechanic, so no uncapped increase right exists to cap.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered: "unless terminated by the Company upon sixty (60), or by HDI upon ninety (90), days written notice to the other." The shared noun phrase "days written notice" applies to both figures, so the Company's (Customer's) window is 60 days. The deterministic check reported "number not found" only because the numeral is separated from the word "days" by the inserted HDI clause; substantively the 60-day ceiling is satisfied.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition not engaged: the fee is a fixed 30% revenue share and neither Section 4.1 nor any other cited provision permits a renewal price increase, so no cap language is required.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the Company's non-renewal notice window is reduced from ninety (90) to sixty (60) days, and the price-increase element is inapplicable because the Agreement carries a fixed 30% revenue share with no renewal uplift mechanic.
The 'deviation' classification of the original clause is correct: the pre-edit 90-day mutual window sat at the walk-away threshold and failed the 60-day fallback ceiling.

Minimality holds. The only substantive change is the numeral governing the Company's notice; HDI's ninety-day window is retained rather than shortened, which preserves existing Customer-favourable friction on Vendor exit. No survival tails, procedures, reminder mechanics or uplift caps were added beyond the fallback checklist.

Intent is preserved: the one-year initial term, the automatic one-year renewal, the 'to the other' notice direction and the retained sentence defining the "Termination Date" all survive without contradiction, and no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling.

Drafting nit only (not a defect requiring repair): the split construction "upon sixty (60), or by HDI upon ninety (90), days written notice" caused the deterministic window regex to miss the figure. Consider rendering it as "unless terminated by the Company upon sixty (60) days' written notice, or by HDI upon ninety (90) days' written notice, to the other" so the operative period is unambiguous on its face.

Preferred position remains unmet on three points the comment correctly concedes: no mutual-written-agreement renewal, a 60- rather than 30-day Customer opt-out, and no Vendor renewal reminder at least 60 days before each renewal. Under the playbook these are noted in the rationale, not separately flagged.
